title: How do you build a training matrix for a food business?
seoTitle: Training matrix for a food business
description: Build a food business training matrix: handler, supervisor, PCQI and alcohol service duties by market, certificate expiry, premises coverage and records.
shortAnswer: A food business training matrix lists each food role (handler, supervisor or person in charge, manager, preventive controls lead, harvest worker, bar staff) against the food safety and liquor rules of the market where each premises operates, then records the certificate each role needs, when that certificate expires, and the record an inspector will ask to see. Unlike most matrices, it must also check that every premises and shift has a qualified supervisor present or reachable.
keyTakeaways: Food rules attach to premises and shifts as well as to people, so the matrix needs a coverage view alongside the usual person view.
Supervisor and alcohol service certificates expire on fixed cycles: five years for NSW food safety supervisors and NSW RSA cards, three years for Victorian RSA refreshers.

Many food handler duties set no refresher interval. FSANZ and the European Commission both leave frequency to the business, while the FSMA Produce Safety Rule requires training on hiring and at least annually.
Inspectors check records on site: Victorian venues must produce RSA certificates immediately, NSW premises must hold a copy of the supervisor certificate.
Manufacturing and farm sites in the United States add qualified individual roles under 21 CFR parts 117 and 112.

sections.heading: What makes a food business training matrix different?

blocks.text: Two things: food law ties supervisor duties to a place and a time, and many of the qualifications are external certificates with expiry dates. A [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) that only tracks whether each employee finished a course will miss a kitchen that ran a Saturday shift with no qualified person available.

The rule under Standard 3.2.2A of the Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code shows the pattern. Section 3.2.2A-11 requires a category one or two business to appoint a food safety supervisor who is reasonably available, and section 3.2.2A-10 requires food handlers in a prescribed activity to have completed a food safety training course, or have commensurate skills and knowledge, before they start that activity ([Standard 3.2.2A](/regulations/food-safety-standard-3-2-2a-training)). The first is a coverage rule; the second is a person rule. The matrix needs both.

The base method is in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix). This page adapts it for restaurants, caterers, retailers, licensed venues, food manufacturers and produce farms.

sections.heading: Which food roles belong on the matrix?

blocks.text: Use roles that the food and liquor rules themselves name, because each carries a distinct credential. A cook and a waiter may share an employer but not a requirement set.

items: **Food handler.** Under EU Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, Annex II Chapter XII, food handlers must be supervised and instructed or trained in food hygiene commensurate with their work ([EU food hygiene](/regulations/eu-food-hygiene-training-requirements)). The Commission Notice on food safety management uses the contrast between a waiter and a cook to show that training need differs by activity.

**Food safety supervisor (Australia).** A person holding a certificate issued within the preceding five years from a registered training organization or recognized body, with authority to direct safe food handling. NSW and Queensland add their own rules ([NSW supervisor](/regulations/nsw-food-safety-supervisor-requirements), [Queensland supervisor](/regulations/queensland-food-safety-supervisor-requirements)).

**Person in charge (United States).** FDA Food Code 2-101.11(A) requires a person in charge present during all hours of operation, and 2-102.12(A) requires that person to be a certified food protection manager, unless the regulatory authority deems the establishment minimal risk ([FDA Food Code](/regulations/fda-food-code-certified-food-protection-manager)).

**Food hygiene manager (Japan).** Appended Table 17 of the Food Sanitation Act Enforcement Regulation requires operators to appoint a food hygiene manager (shokuhin eisei sekininsha) ([Japan Food Sanitation Act](/regulations/japan-food-sanitation-act-haccp-and-food-hygiene-manager)).

**HACCP lead.** People responsible for HACCP based procedures need HACCP training under EU Annex II Chapter XII; in US registered food facilities, the food safety plan is prepared or overseen by a preventive controls qualified individual (PCQI) under 21 CFR 117.126(a)(2) ([FSMA PCQI](/regulations/fsma-preventive-controls-qualified-individual-training)).

**Farm harvest worker and supervisor (United States).** Covered farms train personnel who handle covered produce, and at least one supervisor or responsible party must complete training equivalent to an FDA recognized standardized curriculum ([FSMA Produce Safety Rule](/regulations/fsma-produce-safety-rule-worker-training)).

**Alcohol service staff and licensees (Australia).** Anyone who sells, serves or supplies alcohol in NSW needs an RSA competency card; in Victoria, staff at general, on-premises, late night and packaged liquor venues need a current RSA certificate ([NSW RSA](/regulations/responsible-service-of-alcohol-training-nsw), [Victoria RSA](/regulations/responsible-service-of-alcohol-training-victoria)).

blocks.text: The two year refresher for the Sydney barista and the annual cycle for the California line operator are business choices, labelled as such. Neither rule sets them. Recording which intervals are legal and which are chosen keeps the business honest when it reports compliance.

sections.heading: How do you check that every premises and shift is covered?

blocks.text: Add a coverage view: premises down one axis, trading hours or shifts across the other, and in each cell the name of a qualified supervisor or person in charge. Any empty cell is a breach even if every individual's record is current.

items: **List premises and mobile units separately.** In NSW a food safety supervisor must not act for any other premises or mobile catering business, so two cafes need two supervisors.
**Map roster to qualification.** The FDA Food Code expects a person in charge present during all hours of operation; a late shift with no certified manager is a gap.
**Test availability.** Standard 3.2.2A and Queensland s87 require the supervisor to be reasonably available to staff and to the regulator. Record how that is achieved: on site, or easily contactable.

**Wire in change events.** Queensland requires notice to the local government within 14 days when a supervisor starts or stops. Resignations should create a coverage alert and a notification task at once.
**Repeat for alcohol.** NSW licensees, approved managers and club secretaries granted a new license or transfer complete Licensee Training within 60 days; schedule it as a premises level cell.

blocks.title: Why this matters in penalties
blocks.text: In NSW, a licensee who permits staff without an RSA endorsement faces a $1,100 penalty notice under clause 63(2) of the Liquor Regulation 2018. In Victoria, failing to keep staff RSA certificates carries an infringement of $105 and a maximum of $1,046. In Queensland, each supervisor offence under ss86 to 88 carries a maximum of 50 penalty units.

sections.heading: What training records will a food inspector ask to see?

blocks.text: Inspectors usually ask on site, so the evidence must be at the premises or retrievable there. Retention periods vary widely by market.

items: **Australia.** Category one businesses keep substantiating records under section 3.2.2A-12 for 3 months. NSW premises hold a copy of the supervisor certificate. Victorian licensees keep each staff member's current RSA certificate at the venue, no more than 3 years old.
**United States, manufacturing.** 21 CFR 117.180(d) requires PCQI training records showing the date, type of training and person trained; 117.315 keeps records at least 2 years after preparation.
**United States, farms.** 21 CFR 112.30(b) records the date, topics covered and persons trained; 112.164 keeps them at least 2 years.
**United States, retail.** Food Code 2-103.11(P) requires employees to be informed in a verifiable manner of their reporting responsibility, which needs a signed or logged record.

**European Union.** Article 5(2)(g) of Regulation 852/2004 calls for records commensurate with the nature and size of the business, and Article 5(4) requires evidence to be given to the competent authority.
**Japan.** Table 17 item 13 expects periodic verification of training effectiveness and revision, so keep the review, not only attendance.

blocks.text: See [how long to keep training records](/guides/how-long-to-keep-training-records) for a cross industry view and [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) for sampling.

sections.heading: How often should food handlers be retrained when the law is silent?

blocks.text: Retrain on evidence of need and on change, and document the rationale. Food Standards Australia New Zealand (FSANZ) states that no specific refresher period has been set for food handler training and that regular refreshers are best practice.

The European Commission's 2022 notice says refresher frequency should follow needs and demonstrated skills, and that training need not be a formal course. Chapter XIa on food safety culture, added by Regulation (EU) 2021/382, expects appropriate training and supervision. Practical triggers include a new menu item with a new allergen, a new piece of equipment, an inspection finding, or the 2026 FDA Food Code changes that added food defense awareness at 2-103.11(R). A [verification of competency](/glossary/verification-of-competency) check by the supervisor is often better evidence than another online module.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each food role to the hazards, procedures and certificates that justify its requirements, so a change to a HACCP plan or an allergen procedure identifies which handlers and supervisors need reassessment. See [operational procedures](/programs/operational-procedures).

faqs.q: Does every food business in Australia need a food safety supervisor?
faqs.a: No. Standard 3.2.2A requires one for category one and category two businesses, which handle unpackaged, potentially hazardous, ready to eat food. NSW lists exemptions, including Food Authority licensed businesses, manufacture or wholesale only operations, and coffee vans that only heat milk.

faqs.q: Is a US food protection manager certificate the same as food handler training?
faqs.a: No. Food Code 2-102.12 requires the person in charge to be a certified food protection manager who passed a test in an accredited program, and Annex 3 notes that accreditation refers to the certification, not training. General employee training under 2-103.11(O), including food allergy awareness, is a separate requirement for all staff.

faqs.q: Can a new bartender start work before finishing RSA training?
faqs.a: It depends on the state. In Victoria, staff may complete RSA within one month of first supplying alcohol. In NSW, an interim certificate valid for 90 days lets a person work immediately after completing the course while the card is issued. The matrix should hold a different start rule per state.

faqs.q: Do seasonal and contract farm workers need training?
faqs.a: Yes, on covered farms in the United States. 21 CFR 112.21 applies to temporary, part time, seasonal and contracted personnel, with training upon hiring and at least once a year, in a form that is easily understood. Buyers often check supplier records as part of their own controls.
